author: codex:engineering
context: ADR-0031 injected boundary could not interrupt an arbitrary blocked generator. Continuation implements process supervision without modifying historical candidate/runner/defaults.
decision: Keep domain core and historical runners intact. Require source/runtime/command freeze and a new exact outer human execution authorization before any worker. Establish containment before delivering work, persist debit/receipts, stop at first failure and independently replay transport versus semantic results.

evidence.note: 36 synthetic tests use real local Python subprocesses, including timeout and descendant termination. Provider replaced or request rejected before dispatch. Zero real inference calls; no model quality, hermetic environment or real-time guarantee.

limitations: Synthetic local subprocess behavior is not provider schema compatibility or semantic model qualification.
Process launch, I/O and OS scheduling are not hard real-time; trusted workers are required, not a hostile-code sandbox.
POSIX descendants that leave the process group are outside containment; root reaping is observed, not all descendants.
Source freeze and Python version are not a hermetic environment, CLI binary identity or authenticated remote model.
Worker invocations do not count hidden provider requests. No new real-call budget, migration of approvals, default promotion or sprint completion.
review_note: Refresh changed current-source pointers only; immutable earlier revisions retain original evidence. Historical execution requires its frozen source package, not current routing; no requalification or budget transfer.
summary: Opt-in source-frozen transport supervises one fixed JSON worker per charged stage, with monotonic call/session budgets, cleanup reserve, Windows Job Object/POSIX session, durable attempts/receipts and offline replay. New authorization covers exact outer policy and nested flow.
